testbench.name: comparator-regeneration
testbench.description: Decision time versus input overdrive over PVT at 50 mV / 1 mV / 0.1 mV, the regeneration time constant tau extracted from the two small rungs, the near-metastable behaviour at 0.1 mV, and the switching energy and static current per decision.
testbench.claim: sim/dut.json binds design/comparator.spice (id comparator-dr0001, provenance schematic), the ratified topology from spec/decision-records/0001-comparator-topology.md ('DR-0001'). This record substantiates that a three-overdrive transient regeneration sweep genuinely runs and tau is genuinely extracted from it, on that design, over the full PVT grid. Unlike the offset-MC and preamp-noise benches, this bench is transient and unaffected by DR-0001 Decision Section 3's DC-resolvable-front-end finding -- but it is STILL NOT evidence toward README.md#target-specification's Decision-time-vs-overdrive row: that ratification is a separate, later act (spec/porting-plan.md's third step in this chain).

td_od50_ns.description: PRIMARY CORNER-SENSITIVITY ANCHOR as well as the row-facing number. The min/max pair is a sanity envelope, not the spec bound: 1 ps would mean the delay measurement latched onto a numerical artefact, and 25 ns is most of the strobe window. The SPEC bound (README.md's decision-time row) is deliberately NOT encoded while README.md's target-specification table stays DRAFT/unratified (ratification is spec/porting-plan.md's separate third step). The per-axis floors are what make --sabotage-corners fail: regeneration speed is set by device transconductance, which is corner- and temperature-sensitive. The process floor (1.5) is still the value originally calibrated from this experiment's first committed 45-point record (named in this experiment's README.md, run --no-write during issue #8 development, taken against the then-bound placeholder DUT), ~40% margin below that record's observed weakest process slice (2.61%); it still holds against the real DR-0001 DUT (sim/dut.json now binds design/comparator.spice), whose own weakest observed process slice is 25.16% (record sim/comparator-regeneration/records/20260916-021945-36773c7.json). The temperature floor was RECALIBRATED (issue #16): the placeholder-derived value (8.0, ~40% margin below that placeholder record's observed weakest temperature slice of 12.76%) FAILED against the real DUT's own weakest observed temperature slice of 2.73% (same record) -- physically plausible, not a plumbing bug: regeneration speed is set by transconductance, which falls with temperature, but falling V_th raises the effective overdrive at the same time, so the real transistor-level latch's decision time partially cancels its own temperature dependence to first order (the same kind of first-order cancellation this bench's sibling check, comparator-preamp-noise's av_dc process floor, documents for its own axis). The new floor (1.5) is recalibrated from that same real-DUT record, ~45% margin below its observed weakest temperature slice (2.729%); see design/README.md's 'Open items' for the resolution note. The supply axis is unfloored because the delay threshold is supply-normalized on purpose (see the deck header), which removes most of the supply dependence from the measurement by construction (observed weakest supply slice: 2.02%).

tau_ps.description: Regeneration time constant, extracted from the (1 mV, 0.1 mV) pair -- both inside the logarithmic region, one decade apart, so tau = (t(0.1 mV) - t(1 mV))/ln(10). Bounds are a sanity envelope: a negative or sub-0.1 ps tau means the two delays came out in the wrong order, and 20 ns means the structure is not regenerating on the timescale of the strobe.

resolve_decades.description: How many e-folds of regeneration fit inside the measured 1 mV decision time (td_od1 / tau). It is the metastability lever arm: the probability of an unresolved decision falls as exp(-t/tau), so this is the exponent that number is taken to.

dout_od50_end.description: POLARITY CHECK: after the second strobe the 50 mV instance must hold the POSITIVE answer (dout normalized to its own supply). Together with dout_od50_first below it proves the same instance decided BOTH ways within one run.

dout_od01_end.description: the same at 0.1 mV overdrive -- i.e. the near-metastable rung still resolves to the CORRECT answer within the strobe window, which is the statement the metastability row rests on.

dout_od50_first.description: the OPPOSITE-polarity half of the same proof: at the first strobe the input was negative, so the held output must be low.

i_static_ua.description: Static supply current of one instance with the strobe low. A floor only: zero would mean the bias never came up and every dynamic number in this record was taken on a dead circuit.

e_dec_fj.description: SWITCHING ENERGY PER DECISION, added as a real check now that sim/dut.json binds a transistor-level decision stage (design/comparator.spice) -- see this note's own prior trigger condition in evidence.notes below. abs(q_dec - i_stat*8.1e-9)*vsup_v integrates the supply current over the second-strobe decision window, nets out the static-bias baseline, and converts to energy; the abs() means this is a magnitude sanity envelope, not a spec bound (README.md has no energy-per-decision row). Bounds are deliberately loose (roughly 30x either side of the first transistor-level 45-point record's observed ~31-61 fJ span, named in this experiment's README.md) to catch a wrong-sign/wrong-units/collapsed-to-residue regression, not to pin the design's actual switching energy.
